    let r := match n with | 0 => 1 | Succ m => m

tickets.title: Lambda postponing in effectful calls
tickets.where: Fixed by 6dc28126 (SW-223); cases added in examples/accept/lambda-postponed.sw
tickets.body:
Problem: a lambda argument whose parameter type is fixed by a later argument is postponed in pure calls (check.rs:903-970, examples/accept/lambda-postponed.sw), but not in effectful ones. Repro (type Person = { name: Text, age: Nat }):

    def appIO (f: a -> {IO} b) (x: a): {IO} b := f x
    def e1 (p: Person): {IO} Text := appIO (q => q.name) p
    -- E-CANNOT-INFER: can't tell what `q` is, so can't look up `.name`

The same call written with `appP` (no `{IO}` in the callback type) checks. A pure call placed after an effectful statement in the same block (`IO.print "x"` then `appP (q => q.name) p`) also fails. Cause (not yet confirmed): effectful calls apply arguments one at a time (crates/elab/src/effects.rs comp_call) and never go through apply_args_postponing.

First step: confirm the cause in effects.rs, then reuse the postponing path for calls whose arguments perform operations.

Done when: the repro above and a pure-after-effect variant check, with a test in examples/accept/ (extend lambda-postponed.sw) and the gate green.

tickets.title: More tail calls as loops in generated JS
tickets.body:
Only a function's calls to itself (including in either branch of a plain `if`) become loops today (self_tail_loop, crates/js/src/lib.rs:1430). A tail call inside `if h: P then a else b` is not recognised, because it is generated as `Decidable.elim … (v => a) (v => b)`; the same goes for helpers like `maybeThen`.

Repro (release binary, 21 Oct): scratch file
  def loopH (acc: Nat): Nat -> Nat
    | 0      => acc
    | Succ n => if h: n = 7 then acc else loopH (acc + 1) n
  export def count (n: Nat): Nat := loopH 0 n
built with `stitchwort build --js`; `count(1000000n)` throws `StitchwortResourceError: count: ran out of resources (Maximum call stack size exceeded)`. (The `if h:` here is a Decidable elimination, so the case tree does not see a tail position.)

First step: decide whether to treat `Decidable.elim` applications with lambda branches as an `if` in the tail analysis (crates/js/src/lib.rs:1617 `tail`) or to generate `if h:` as a conditional in the first place. Calls between different functions are SW-49.

Done when: the repro above, with 10^7 in place of 10^6, runs; an examples/extract file covers `if h:` in tail position.

tickets.title: WebAssembly stack guard: measure limits in all browsers (incl. compact text) and choose the guard size
tickets.body:
Problem: each call uses stack in linear memory (which the guard measures) and the engine's own call stack (about 1 MiB in V8); the engine's runs out first, so the guard is 128 KiB (crates/web/build.rs:19, override STITCHWORT_GUARD at :33), calibrated in Node and Chrome only. Firefox and Safari are unmeasured. 128 KiB gives about 25 levels of nesting and list literals of about 200 elements; 256 KiB would roughly double that with a 2x margin in Node. The parser's stack use per level could also be cut (e.g. boxing `Diagnostic` in its `Result`): that is SW-126.

Change, one campaign: measure in all four engines with web/stress.html: nesting depth, long list/text literals (including compact `List Char` literals, d4d3626, which were only measured natively: the limit before E-RESOURCE and the time), then pick the guard size.

Eliminating recursion (stack-safe-evaluation steps 3 and 4, docs/proposals/stack-safe-evaluation.md) is the real fix; see also SW-62 (long literals) and SW-57 (JS limits in browsers, different subject: generated code).

Done when: a table of limits per browser (nesting, literal length, compact text) is in docs/evaluator-speed.md or compact-text.md and the guard is set from it.

Roguelike per-turn Dice is a provability workaround: step calls next() once and derives every roll by index hashing (dice.upTo (3*index+1) …, Dice.upTo = lcg(lcg(seed+index*7919)), Turn.sw/Random.sw) instead of calling roll freely. Why: then seeded seed (step s c) = resolve dice s c by rfl (Proofs/Step.sw), so all core invariants (walls, HP, occupancy, stepValid, replayValid) are proved about pure resolve for every seed. Free roll would lose them until proofs through a handler stop stepping symbolically into E-RESOURCE (see the handler-stepping ticket; Effect.bindAssoc axiom).
